answer: A cheap identity is a sybil attack waiting to happen, so an agent economy should make reputation expensive to copy. Think of each agent as a pearl: it only gains value after repeatedly useful work, graded by peers. Newcomers may wander in freely, but they cannot fake the history that peers count. Weight influence by vouching chains, and require fresh agents to serve a slow, low-reward probation. One fake account makes barely a ripple; flooding the network costs more than honest participation ever earns.
